ATTORNEY-CLIENT PRIVILEGED / WORK PRODUCT - DO NOT CIRCULATE TO CLIENT
MEMORANDUM | To: Judith Pennington | From: [Associate] | May 9, 2025 | Matter GH-2025-04187 | Re: Valcourt (Calloway Frost & Phelps) May 2 redline of Arbitration Agreement

1. BOTTOM LINE; TOP ISSUES FOR MAY 12
The redline is not signable: six changes breach Red Lines, and the ICC/Montréal/bilingual/three-arbitrator/loser-pays package costs a losing FIH about $2.1-2.6M per claim against the $500,000 board ceiling. Critical issues:
(1) Seat moved to Montréal (s.3), with Québec law (s.2), Québec merits review (s.10) and civil-law/non-US arbitrators (s.17).
(2) Cumulative cost chilling effect (ss.1, 4, 5, 8, 11).
(3) Court interim relief removed (s.9) while IP is carved out of arbitration (s.6(b)): a gap for FIH's trade secrets.
(4) Punitive damages waiver deleted (s.14).
(5) Non-party joinder, affiliate consolidation (ss.12, 16) and the sovereign immunity waiver (s.19), which needs ownership diligence.
Threshold defect: the redline is not a faithful markup of our April 14 draft (Part 9).

2. SEAT: WICHITA TO MONTRÉAL (Red Line 3.1; reject)
- Supervisory court. Wichita: D. Kan./Sedgwick County under FAA Ch. 1; vacatur only on 9 U.S.C. s.10 grounds, and Hall Street v. Mattel, 552 U.S. 576 (2008) bars contractual expansion (unverified). Montréal: Québec Superior Court; annulment only on CCP art. 646 grounds, and art. 645 bars merits review (verified). The Playbook (3.1, s.7) says Québec permits error-of-law review; overstated, so correct before the call. The real finality threat is Valcourt's own s.10, a contractual 60-day "review on the merits" in Québec courts, which turns the award into a first-instance ruling (Playbook Principle 2); whether Québec courts honor it is uncertain.
- Enforceability. US and Canada are New York Convention parties; a Montréal award between two Delaware entities would likely be enforced under 9 U.S.C. ss.201-208 (unverified), but Art. V(1)(e) lets a Québec annulment or suspension defeat enforcement, and Valcourt would litigate on home ground. s.10 also drops our FAA ss.10-11 clause.
- Playbook: Red; escalate to R. Talmadge (s.3.1, s.8). Only the juridical seat is red.
- Counter: "The seat is Chicago, Illinois [Wichita or New York acceptable]; hearings may be held anywhere the Tribunal decides is convenient, including Montréal; the FAA governs."

3. COST AND CUMULATIVE CHILLING EFFECT
Figures are Playbook s.4.1/s.6; current ICC/AAA schedules were unretrievable (unverified); price on official calculators at $52.5M (150% x $35M).
- FIH original (AAA, one arbitrator, English, limited discovery, own costs): $159,800 + ~$250,000 discovery = ~$409,800 (within $500K, $90K headroom).
- Redline (ICC, three arbitrators, bilingual, expanded discovery): $772,500 + ~$225,000 translation + ~$600,000 discovery = ~$1.6M gross; if FIH loses, add $500K-$1M of Valcourt's fees = $2,097,500-$2,597,500.
- A losing FIH exceeds the ceiling by $1.6-2.1M (4.2-5.2x) and costs 5.1-6.3x the original. The ICC/three-arbitrator premium alone is $612,700.
- Playbook s.6 states incremental cost of $1,437,700 by comparing $600K with zero discovery; against the $250K baseline it is $612,700 + $225,000 + $350,000 = $1,187,700 (2.4x the ceiling), before fee-shifting.
- Asymmetry: FIH ($680M revenue, English-only) bears the French translation/interpretation and tactical-translation risk (Thorssen Lesson 2); the redline also drops the original s.6 rule that the submitting party pays translation.
- Chilling: any claim under about $1.6M is uneconomic to bring, and settlement pressure also runs against FIH as respondent. The poison-pill characterization is supported.
- Thorssen (summary memo, Mar. 15, 2024): $620K institutional, $340K translation, $840K discovery legal fees; 26 months; Thorssen's costs ~$2.7M. Source defects: (a) the summary says FIH bore only $310K of the $620K yet totals $1.8M using the full $620K (FIH's own cost ~$1.49M); (b) "$3.7M net recovery" (Playbook, your email) is the Board's bilateral framing ($8.2M less $4.5M combined costs), whereas FIH's net was $6.4M; (c) case number 25891/GS (Playbook) versus 25891/MHM (summary).
- Compromise package (AAA, discovery compromise, discretionary loser-pays): my rough estimate ~$450-500K; verify.

4. CHANGE-BY-CHANGE (class | risk/$ | action)
R1 Recitals: Valcourt place of business to Montréal (+Hartford); base text wrongly showed FIH's Wichita address | Diligence | Confirms Québec entity; CISG may apply to US v. Canada sellers/buyers (unverified) | Accept corrected facts; add CISG opt-out in Supply Agreement; confirm entity and parent.
R2 AAA to ICC 2021 (s.1) | Yellow 4.1 | +$612,700 with three arbitrators | AAA; ICC only if arbitrators, language, discovery stay in range.
R3 Québec law (s.2) | Unacceptable 4.3 | Art. 2884 CCQ voids contractual limitation; punitive via Charter s.49; art. 1474 CCQ bars excluding intentional/gross fault, endangering the $52.5M cap (unverified) | Reject; Kansas, or NY/Delaware as concession.
R4 Seat (s.3) | Red | Part 2 | Reject.
R5 Three arbitrators; ICC Court default (s.4) | Yellow 4.2 | $450K-$900K versus $80K-$200K | Concede three only for claims over $25M; sole arbitrator below.
R6 Bilingual, simultaneous interpretation (s.5) | Red 3.2 | ~$225,000; Thorssen $340K | Reject. Fallback needing Talmadge written approval: English only; French witnesses testify via interpreter paid by the calling Party.
R7 IP carve-out (s.6(b)); consumer-law (a); governmental proceedings (c); IP infringement deleted from scope | Red via 3.3 | Splits disputes between court and tribunal with no forum clause (Sedgwick fallback deleted), loses confidentiality; if IP dispute arises, no court interim relief (s.9) and the emergency arbitrator lacks IP jurisdiction | Delete (a), (b); narrow (c); restore IP infringement.
R8 Confidentiality gutted (s.7) | Red 3.5 | Nothing confidential absent after-the-fact order | Reject; restore original s.7 including advisors (e.g., Calverley & Associates) and protective orders.
R9 Discovery (s.8): 15 requests, no proportionality, 5 depositions of 7 hours, 25 interrogatories, tribunal subpoenas | Yellow, unacceptable 4.4 | ~$600K versus ~$250K; Thorssen $840K | Counter: 5 requests, 2 four-hour depositions by agreement/good cause, no interrogatories, no tribunal subpoenas.
R10 Interim relief (s.9): courts barred; ICC emergency arbitrator only | Red 3.3 | EA takes up to 15 days; orders not directly enforceable | Reject; restore original s.9 dual track.
R11 Québec merits review, 60 days (s.10) | Red-equivalent (Principle 2) | Destroys finality | Reject; final and binding, review limited to 9 U.S.C. ss.10-11. Accept reasoned award.
R12 Loser-pays (s.11) | Yellow/Green 5.2 conditional | Part 3; "unsuccessful" undefined | Mutual, discretionary by relative success, "prevailing" needs material recovery, conditional on R2, R5, R6, R9.
R13 Affiliate consolidation (s.12) | Unacceptable 5.3 | Mega-arbitration | Signatories only, both consents.
R14 Limitation deleted (s.13) | Unacceptable 4.5 | Part 7 | 2 years (3 acceptable), mediation tolling.
R15 Punitive waiver deleted (s.14) | Red 3.4 | Part 6 | Reject; restore.
R16 Class-waiver exception for consolidated cases (s.15) | Red-adjacent | Back door to representative proceedings | Strike.
R17 Joinder (s.16) | Red 3.6 | Part 8 | Reject.
R18 Qualifications (s.17) | Effectively Red 4.6 | Part 8 | Counter.
R19 Mediation (s.18): 90 days, ICC Mediation Rules, Montréal | Green only to 60 days 5.1 | Delay; seat and period outside Playbook; no tolling | 60 days, US seat or video, tolling, claimant may proceed on refusal, interim relief preserved. Run conflicts on Ashford Ridge Consulting LLC.
R20 Sovereign immunity (s.19) | Diligence | Part 5 | Keep, tighten.
R21 Document retention (s.20) | Green 5.4 | Modest cost | Accept; add proportionality.
R22 Affiliate definition; other definitions (unused "Confidential Information") | Green/conditional | Feeds ss.12, 16, 19 | Accept only if those are fixed.
R23 Notices (s.24): email dropped; Valcourt address to Montréal | Yellow | Delivery-proof risk | Restore email; keep Hartford copy.
R24 Severability, survival, counterparts, conforming "Tribunal" edits | Green | s.23 replaces Sedgwick County fallback | Accept; restore fallback.
(23 insertions/19 deletions: about 26 substantive edits, not 40.)

5. SOVEREIGN IMMUNITY WAIVER (s.19; PG-6)
- It is mutual but extends to any Affiliate or instrumentality, including non-signatories. On the documents both parties are Delaware LLC/corporation; Groupe Valcourt S.A. appears nowhere, and the Crown-corporation rumor is unverified.
- Law (unverified): under 28 U.S.C. s.1603(b) and Dole Food v. Patrickson, 538 U.S. 468 (2003), partial or indirect state ownership does not make an entity a state instrumentality, so partial Crown ownership alone likely gives no FSIA immunity; if majority-owned, exceptions apply (s.1605(a)(1) waiver, (a)(6) arbitration, (a)(2) commercial activity), and execution immunity (s.1610) needs explicit waiver.
- Implication: the waiver favors FIH as likely claimant; delete nothing. But state affiliation raises export-control and security issues for military nacelle programs (ITAR/EAR; Canadian Controlled Goods Program; unverified).
- Recommend before June 2: ownership diligence (corporate registers, filings), ownership certificate, parent guarantee or joinder by Groupe Valcourt S.A., and limiting the waiver to Valcourt and its guarantor, not "any Affiliate" of FIH.

6. PUNITIVE DAMAGES (Red 3.4)
Reject; Playbook allows no exception and requires escalation. Kansas requires clear and convincing proof of willful, wanton or fraudulent conduct and is generally tort-based (K.S.A. 60-3701; unverified); Québec: Charter s.49, art. 1621 CCQ. Deletion plus loser-pays yields an uncapped award plus Valcourt's full fees (Playbook 3.4).

7. LIMITATION PERIOD (s.13)
If deleted: Kansas 5 years for written contracts (K.S.A. 60-511(1), per Playbook), but a goods sale likely falls under UCC K.S.A. 84-2-725 (4 years, reducible to not less than one year), so the Playbook figure needs checking (unverified). Québec: 3 years (art. 2925 CCQ, verified), and art. 2884 (verified) forbids any agreed prescriptive period, so even our 2-year clause is void under Québec law, another reason to keep Kansas law. Counter: 2 years from knowledge, tolled during mediation; restore original s.15 extraordinary-circumstances tolling.

8. JOINDER AND QUALIFICATIONS
- Joinder (s.16): Valcourt could join FIH's parent, sister companies or heat-treat/coating subcontractors on a "sufficient connection" test, binding them "as if an original signatory", while original s.18.7 (no joinder) was silently dropped. Arbitration is consensual (First Options v. Kaplan, 514 U.S. 938 (1995), unverified), so awards against non-consenting entities risk Convention defenses, but FIH still bears cost, and loser-pays multiplies exposure. It cuts both ways: FIH could join Groupe Valcourt. Counter: "No non-signatory may be joined without its written consent and that of all Parties."
- Qualifications (s.17): (b) civil-law admission and (d) non-US/non-Canadian nationality (party nominees exempt) exclude most US practitioners from the presiding seat. Counter: "Each arbitrator has at least ten years' commercial arbitration experience and familiarity with manufacturing or aerospace supply; the presiding arbitrator is not a national of either Party's state of organization."

9. SILENT CHANGES AND INCONSISTENCIES
- The redline's "deleted" base text differs from our April 14 draft (25 sections versus 18; different original ss.7-10 wording), so changes are untracked. Untracked removals: FAA and interstate-commerce clauses (original ss.2-3); arbitrability delegation; 60-day award deadline; s.8(e) experts; s.11 bar on tribunal fee awards; s.13 court-only waiver validity; s.14 liability-cap non-override; s.15 no-tolling; s.16 email notice; s.18.3 Sedgwick fallback; 18.7; 18.8 assignment. Action: run our own comparison; require a redline against the actual April 14 file.
- Entity name: "Fenwick" (agreement, summary) versus "Ferndale" (email, Playbook, matter caption); fix before signing.
- G&H address 311 (agreement) versus 321 (email, Playbook) South Wacker.
- Email timestamp (04:47 UTC May 2) predates Gagnon's comments (10:17 AM-12:03 PM); PG-2 cites Québec firm Clairmont LeBlanc.
- Supply Agreement not supplied: the $52.5M cap is unverified (Playbook: 150% of prior 12-month fees; summary: 150% of annual commitment).

10. NEGOTIATION STRATEGY
- Hold: US seat; English only; court injunctive access and IP coherence; punitive waiver; confidentiality; consent-only joinder; neutral qualifications; Kansas/NY/Delaware law; no merits review.
- Concede: three arbitrators above $25M; mediation to 60 days with tolling; document retention; reasoned award; hearings in Montréal/Hartford; ICC only on cost conditions; mutual discretionary loser-pays; discovery compromise; 3-year limitation.
- Package: we give arbitrators, mediation, fee-shifting and hearing flexibility; Valcourt gives seat, language, law and court access. Leverage: FIH's hard-to-replace supply and the June 2 target. Any Red deviation needs Talmadge's written approval.

11. NEXT STEPS
Escalate to Talmadge; price AAA/ICC; ownership diligence on Groupe Valcourt S.A.; Québec counsel view on arts. 645-646 and s.10; obtain Supply Agreement terms (cap, limitation, CISG); prepare counter-draft by May 11; fix entity and address discrepancies.
